hypotheses.claim: Relation-instance/n-ary identity is necessary when group/role semantics are not proven reducible.
hypotheses.counter: Weighted pairwise semantics suffice for all target FRANK relations.
hypotheses.falsifier: A proven pairwise lowering preserves all role/query/effect semantics across the target corpus.

hypotheses.claim: Naive entity-pair flattening produces increasing false completions as n-ary relation density rises.
hypotheses.counter: Pairwise flattening remains sufficiently selective at target densities.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target ClayGraph traces show no material ambiguity increase.

hypotheses.claim: Typed relation-node/incidence lowering can substitute for native hyperedges when exact n-ary identity is preserved.
hypotheses.counter: Native hyperedges are required for correctness/performance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Relation-node lowering fails semantic equivalence or target cost gates.

hypotheses.claim: Some higher-order operations admit exact weighted pairwise reduction; H5 should compile to the simplest proven-equivalent topology.
hypotheses.counter: Higher-order structure is irreducible by default.
hypotheses.falsifier: No useful target operation class passes an equivalence proof.

hypotheses.claim: Representation order and propagation strength/depth are independent design variables.
hypotheses.counter: Richer representation necessarily requires stronger propagation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target utility is monotonic only under coupled representation/propagation changes.

hypotheses.claim: Unbounded multi-way activation increases irrelevant spread faster than bounded context-gated propagation on mixed-context ClayGraph.
hypotheses.counter: Learned weights alone prevent overspread.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unbounded target runs match or beat gated utility/noise/cost.

hypotheses.claim: Hard gating can become brittle; a bounded cross-context diversity reserve improves recovery/OOD without excessive noise.
hypotheses.counter: Strict context isolation is always best.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reserve never improves OOD/recovery at equal cost/noise.

hypotheses.claim: Utility-adapted salience without gain/inhibition/diversity controls can create self-reinforcing wrong attractors.
hypotheses.counter: Immutable truth alone prevents cognitive attractors.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial utility poisoning produces no persistent selection distortion.

hypotheses.claim: Context-active dependency sets reduce false invalidation versus static union of all contextual alternatives.
hypotheses.counter: Static union cost is negligible or beneficial.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target traces show no meaningful reject/recompute savings.

hypotheses.claim: Context-scoped invalidation is safe only when closure is KNOWN; UNKNOWN must broaden/escalate.
hypotheses.counter: Narrow observed scope is sufficient under hidden dependencies.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial hidden-dependency suite yields no unsafe accepts.

hypotheses.claim: Recovery should replay canonical events rather than treat derived propagation state as authority.
hypotheses.counter: Derived state replay is equally reliable and cheaper.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fault injection shows equivalent recovery integrity.

hypotheses.claim: TCQS collection semantics changes candidate topology before GWT and belongs in topology/selection identity.
hypotheses.counter: Collection algebra differences are implementation detail.
hypotheses.falsifier: Typed-vs-erased target queries preserve candidate membership/rank.

hypotheses.claim: System WorkspaceEpisode and model-internal workspace form separate causal topology levels.
hypotheses.counter: A single workspace variable explains both.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target mediation shows no independent internal uptake stage.

hypotheses.claim: Physical transport topology has a payload/platform threshold; no single IPC path is universally optimal.
hypotheses.counter: Shared memory or same-process handles universally dominate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target benchmark shows one route dominates all relevant payloads/fault regimes.

hypotheses.claim: Physical colocation reduces some handoff costs but increases common-mode failure radius for authority/untrusted domains.
hypotheses.counter: Full monolith is both fastest and acceptably safe.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fault/security tests show no meaningful blast-radius cost.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic topology can remain invariant while physical topology changes if receipts/order semantics are preserved.
hypotheses.counter: Physical placement changes cognition semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: Differential lowering changes outputs despite semantic-equivalence receipts.

hypotheses.claim: Incremental maintenance wins when the change frontier is sparse, but always-incremental is suboptimal once overlay/read tax grows.
hypotheses.counter: One maintenance policy dominates.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target workload shows no crossover.

hypotheses.claim: Revocation should follow active ancestry rather than globally invalidate all contextual alternatives when closure is known.
hypotheses.counter: Global invalidation is necessary for safety.
hypotheses.falsifier: Scoped ancestry misses target-dependent revoked descendants.

hypotheses.claim: Higher-order/critical-like dynamics are not sufficient emergence evidence; E-CERT2 remains required.
hypotheses.counter: Stable higher-order dynamics alone establish emergent organization.
hypotheses.falsifier: None accepted without changing the project's scientific definition; test concerns sufficiency under E-CERT2.

hypotheses.claim: A target-Qwen factorial crossing representation, propagation, system/internal workspace and re-entry can isolate functional Hyperposition benefit beyond retrieval/projection confounds.
hypotheses.counter: No separable Hyperposition contribution exists.
hypotheses.falsifier: All isolated effects vanish or are explained by visible-information/projection controls.
